title: Bread, French or Vienna, whole wheat

content.title: About
content.content: Whole‑wheat French or Vienna bread is made from whole wheat flour, a natural sourdough starter, and a modest amount of salt. It features a crisp crust, aromatic crumb, and a subtle tang typical of sourdough breads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional French (baguette) and Viennese loaves are often baked in steam ovens, giving them a crunchy crust.
Whole‑wheat flour retains the bran and germ, making the bread more nutritious than white flour breads.
The sourdough starter contains live lactic‑acid bacteria that enhance flavor and extend shelf life.
In France and Austria, bread is a cultural staple and is served with virtually every meal.
Whole‑wheat bread has a lower glycemic index than white bread because carbohydrates are released more slowly.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole‑wheat bread provides dietary fiber that supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Whole grains supply iron, magnesium, and zinc, important for blood formation and immune support.

items.title: Supports gut microbiota
items.content: Live cultures from the sourdough can help foster beneficial bacteria in the intestine.

items.title: Lower glycemic impact
items.content: Compared with white bread, whole‑wheat varieties cause a slower rise in blood sugar levels.

items.title: Wheat allergy or celiac disease
items.content: People with wheat allergy or celiac disease should avoid this bread as it can trigger adverse reactions.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Some recipes contain a noticeable amount of salt; individuals monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While healthier than white bread, it still provides calories; portion control is advisable for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bread works well for sandwiches, toast, serving alongside soups and salads, or as a base for bruschetta. It can be toasted, used for croutons, breadcrumb coating, or as an open‑face snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the loaf in a paper bag or linen cloth at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag – it retains flavor and texture for up to 2 months. Thaw and warm in the oven before serving.
